name: settings-page
title: Settings page
purpose: A screen of settings shown defaults first: the few settings most people change, one advanced disclosure holding the rest, and a marked danger area for actions that destroy something.
whenToUse: For the settings of one thing, such as a repository, a runner or an account, when a few of them are changed often and the rest rarely.
Save-on-change: every control saves the moment it changes. Use switches and selects, say so in the page description, and give the page no primary action.
Explicit save: the settings take effect together. Make the page a form with checkboxes in place of switches, and one primary button that names what it saves.
whenNotToUse: For one or two settings that belong to a view. Put a switch or a select in that view.
For a task with an order to it, such as connecting a repository. Use the multi-step form.
For settings in several unrelated groups, each long enough to scroll. Give each group a screen of its own, linked from the sidebar nav, and use this pattern on each.
For facts the reader cannot change. Use a key-value list.

variants.name: save on change
variants.use: Each control saves as it changes. The page description says so, a failed save is reported on the control that failed, and there is no primary button.

variants.name: explicit save
variants.use: The page is one form. Its primary button, written last in a button group after a secondary Discard changes, is the only primary action, and a status line above it says what is not saved yet.

accessibility: In an app the element with gw-settings-page is the main element. The examples use a div because a gallery page holds several of them.
The page title is the h1, in a page header. Each group of settings starts with an h2, and the danger area is a card whose title is an h2 that says Danger area and what it belongs to.

Every setting keeps the markup of its own component: a switch for a setting saved at once, a checkbox inside a form, a select or a text input in a field. Each has a visible label, and a default is already chosen.
For a setting written as one row, with its label and description at the start and its control at the far end, use the settings row component.

There is exactly one details element with data-gw-advanced in the view. Its summary reads Advanced settings and counts what is inside in a gw-disclosure__meta span. It starts closed, and nothing the reader must set before the page works goes inside it.

Every action in the danger area carries data-gw-critical and gw-button--danger, is visible without opening anything, and sits beside a sentence that says what is lost. Ask before it runs with a confirm dialog.
Save-on-change: when a save fails, set the control back and add its component's error element with role="alert", saying which state the setting is in and what to do.

Explicit save: the line that says what is unsaved has role="status". While the form is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button and change its label to Saving settings. Report a failed save in an alert above the button group.

While the settings load, a skeleton stands in for the groups, with aria-busy="true" and a gw-visually-hidden line that says what is loading. If they cannot be loaded, show an error state in its place.
Tab moves through the settings in reading order, then the advanced summary, then the danger area. The pattern needs no script of its own.
